Q: Scan directories and copy those that have more than n files A:

I love python, but the OP problem statement seems a natural fit for find.

#! /usr/bin/env bash

# Copies artist song folders,
# if their song count is above some threshold.

# The OP suggested an example threshold of seven songs per artist.
thresh="{$1:-7}"
dst="{$2:-/mnt/sdcard/musiclight}"
src="."
tmp="/tmp"

get_artist_folders() {
  find "${src}" -type f |
    sed -e "s;\./;;" -e "s;/.*;;" |
    sort |
    uniq -c |
    tee "${tmp}/artist-count.txt" |
    sort -n -r |
    awk '$1 > '${thresh}' {print $2}'
}

rsync -av "$(get_artist_folders)" "${dst}/"

Instead of -type f we might prefer an expression like -name "*.mp3" -o -name "*.mp4". The idea is to identify the relevant song files.

The sed strips the path suffix, leaving just e.g. "artist3". We don't have to strip the prefix -- leaving it as "./artist3" would be fine, if perhaps slightly more ugly. In which case something like awk -F/ '{print $2}' or cut -d/ -f 2 would probably be more convenient than modifying the sed command.

As is usual for such pipelines, you might find the tee result is a convenient debugging aid, to better understand exactly which artists are being considered for copying.

And then of course rsync is very good at recursively grabbing subtrees and copying both data and metadata, so timestamps and permissions will be preserved. Notice that if you have album cover art or other non-song metadata within an artist folder, that will be copied over as well. Consider that a bug or a feature, as you wish.

Q: Get size of all tables in database A: 
SELECT 
    t.name AS TableName, s.name AS SchemaName, p.rows,
    CAST(ROUND(((SUM(a.total_pages) * 8) / 1024.00), 2) AS NUMERIC(36, 2)) AS TotalSpaceMB,
    CAST(ROUND(((SUM(a.total_pages) * 8) / 1024.00 / 1024.00), 2) AS NUMERIC(36, 2)) AS TotalSpaceGB,
    CAST(ROUND(((SUM(a.used_pages) * 8) / 1024.00), 2) AS NUMERIC(36, 2)) AS UsedSpaceMB, 
    CAST(ROUND(((SUM(a.used_pages) * 8) / 1024.00 / 1024.00), 2) AS NUMERIC(36, 2)) AS UsedSpaceGB, 
    CAST(ROUND(((SUM(a.total_pages) - SUM(a.used_pages)) * 8) / 1024.00, 2) AS NUMERIC(36, 2)) AS UnusedSpaceMB,
    CAST(ROUND(((SUM(a.total_pages) - SUM(a.used_pages)) * 8) / 1024.00 / 1024.00, 2) AS NUMERIC(36, 2)) AS UnusedSpaceGB
FROM 
    sys.tables t
INNER JOIN      
    sys.indexes i ON t.object_id = i.object_id
INNER JOIN 
    sys.partitions p ON i.object_id = p.object_id AND i.index_id = p.index_id
INNER JOIN 
    sys.allocation_units a ON p.partition_id = a.container_id
LEFT OUTER JOIN 
    sys.schemas s ON t.schema_id = s.schema_id
WHERE 
    t.name NOT LIKE 'dt%' 
    AND t.is_ms_shipped = 0
    AND i.object_id > 255 
GROUP BY 
    t.name, s.name, p.rows
ORDER BY 
    TotalSpaceMB DESC, t.name

Q: How to find d, given p, q, and e in RSA? A:

Taken the values p=7, q=11 and e=17. then the value of n=p*q=77 and f(n)=(p-1)(q-1)=60. Therefore, our public key pair is,(e,n)=(7,77) Now for calvulating the value of d we have the constraint,

e*d == 1 mod (f(n)), [here "==" represents the **congruent symbol**].
17*d == 1 mod 60
(17*53)*d == 53 mod 60, [7*53=901, which gives modulus value 1]
1*d == 53 mod 60

hence,this gives the value of d=53. Therefore our private key pair will be, (d,n)=(53,77).

Q: Unable to retrieve project metadata. Ensure it's an MSBuild-based .NET Core project. (Migrations) A:

I ran into this again in 2026 and this time the reason was a drifting dotnet-ef version to my project's dotnet version. So my project is dotnet7 and dotnet ef --version showed me v10.

So seemingly dotnet-ef is not super compatible between dotnet versions but you can freeze it for your project.

dotnet new tool-manifest
dotnet tool install dotnet-ef --version 7.0.20
dotnet tool restore

For the right version check https://www.nuget.org/packages/dotnet-ef and select the versions tab and take the highest version of your dotnet version.

Also make sure you use the right type of / (see my first answer) and that you are in the right folder and paths are correct.

Q: Store a value, adding 1 and use it in an insert using Db2 A:

Just stumbled on this and thought this might work for you. Just a straight insert into the table based on your code above. Not sure how this would not give you a duplicate key assuming the key on the table is T1CATEGORIA, T1SEDE, T1CERTIFICATO.

This seems like it should just be an update to the T1PROG column, code below the Insert.

Insert Into MySchema.MyTable (T1CATEGORIA, T1SEDE, T1CERTIFICATO, T1PROG)
(Select
    T1CATEGORIA
    ,T1SEDE
    ,T1CERTIFICATO
    ,Max(T1PROG) + 1
From
    MySchema.MyTable
Where
    T1CATEGORIA = 'abc'
    And T1SEDE = 'abcd'
    And T1CERTIFICATO = 'numCertPe'
);

Update MySchema.MyTable t
Set T1PROG = (
        Select
            Max(T1PROG) + 1
        From
            MySchema.MyTable mt
        Where
            t.T1CATEGORIA = mt.T1CATEGORIA
            And t.T1SEDE = mt.T1SEDS
            And t.T1CERTIFICATO = mt.T1CERTIFICATO
        )
Where
    t.T1CATEGORIA = 'abc'
    And t.T1SEDE = 'abcd'
    And t.T1CERTIFICATO = 'numCertPe'
;
